title: When the Drama Is Your Mama: Setting Boundaries with Parents and In-Laws, Grandparents, and Other Family Members
coreMove: Family love does not grant unlimited access; boundaries protect parenting, bodies, homes, visits, and holidays so connection can continue without old roles running the house.

exampleSpecs.audience: adult children who avoid family after parenting criticism
exampleSpecs.stakes: protect contact with parents by closing the co-parenting debate
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a visit becoming possible only after co-parenting advice gets a clear limit.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who brace for appearance comments at gatherings
exampleSpecs.stakes: stop body scrutiny without turning the whole meal into a trial
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a mother-in-law's weight, clothes, and makeup comments to show a zero-access topic.

exampleSpecs.audience: households whose relatives treat closeness as automatic entry
exampleSpecs.stakes: protect home space while staying civil at the door
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn a surprise visit from in-laws into an advance-notice boundary.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who say yes until family time turns resentful
exampleSpecs.stakes: convert guilt into a sustainable amount of contact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the magic-number approach to choose how much family participation is sustainable.

exampleSpecs.audience: parents who notice body comments hurting a child
exampleSpecs.stakes: respond after a family comment without normalizing appearance scrutiny
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show that appearance comments damage trust even when relatives call them honesty.

exampleSpecs.audience: adults whose relatives still treat the home as shared family space
exampleSpecs.stakes: reclaim home access without arguing about love
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show adult authority over home access as a consent issue, not a family loyalty test.
